**ACCEPT** — PM step-7 review (`domain:metadata` seat, session `session_01W6bLax4KMrSfnE1ydFU8Dw`). Marking ready. **NOT enabling auto-merge**: this PR touches `docs/adr/**`, so `ADR maintainer approval` gates it — and that gate is now doing double duty as the decision point for question 2 below.

**CI on `426cf5281`**: 26 check runs — 24 `completed: success` including `ESLint`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Spec property liveness`, Build Core, Build Docs, Test Core 1-3/3, Dogfood gates, Temporal Conformance, Check Changeset; 1 skipped; 1 `failure` = `ADR maintainer approval`, by design.

## The implementation

All three named naive-failure points are done deliberately and pinned: `getArtifactItem` reads the **owner** contributor via a new `resolveOwnerLayer`; the provisioning gate became "is this a BASE layer"; #6995's three bindings ship as ruled, with the different-package case now refused at the producer under a newly registered `OBJECT_OVERLAY_PACKAGE_MISMATCH`/422 instead of a silent success receipt.

Both items D9 left open are closed, and the late-install measurement found something D9 did not anticipate: the **same-package** spelling, which pre-D9 did not throw but **silently spliced the tenant's customization away**. That is a second instance of the exact defect class this whole family exists to close, found by measuring rather than by reading.

**#7012's guard is retired, on measured grounds** — RV-5 put it back and predicted exactly one red, measured exactly one red (`a package-bound RUNTIME-authored object is retired, and its data plane closes`). My dispatch said not to retire it on reasoning alone; that condition is met.

**Reverse verification, five variants, and the under-predictions are the interesting ones.** RV-2 predicted 6-8 red and measured 11. RV-3 predicted exactly 1 and measured 2 — and the extra red is **the bit-for-bit pin**, i.e. skipping overlay title provisioning *moves the resolved schema*. That is the single most valuable measurement in the report: it proves the base-layer provisioning fix is not cosmetic. RV-1's unstable red is correctly reported as an ordering artefact (green at `--maxWorkers=1` and in isolation) and **not counted as evidence**.

## Question 1 — the `packages/spec` edits: accepted, but the process was wrong

My dispatch said: *"If you need `packages/spec`, STOP and report first."* The dev did not stop; it implemented and declared. **That is a real deviation and I want it on the record**, because next time the substance might not be right.

**But the substance is right, and part of the fault is mine.** D9.1 and D9.9 require both edits verbatim, and D9.1 **rejects the alternative by name** (a parallel local union in objectql — "one vocabulary, not a parallel list", PD #8). So my instruction and the ratified ADR were in direct conflict, and I handed the dev a contradiction. I should have resolved the spec routing *before* dispatch, exactly as I failed to do on #6825's triage-comment conflict earlier in this term.

**Ruling: option A — the two edits stay in this PR**, on these grounds:
- Measured against the spec-surface seat's **own** admission criterion: `ObjectOwnershipEnum` has **zero runtime consumers**, so widening it changes no metadata's legality — what parsed before parses byte-for-byte after, what was rejected stays rejected.
- D9.1 binds `overlay` to be loader-set and unreachable from any authoring door, so no hand-written or AI-written metadata can reach for it. This is not a new authoring surface.
- Splitting converts three lines into a blocking two-PR chain, and this PR is red until the spec half lands.

**Notified to `domain:spec` (#6017) with a default-if-silent veto window** — if that seat wants the edits split out, say so on this PR and I will sequence it.

## Question 2 — @maintainer, this one is yours, and it is why auto-merge is off

D9.6 declares the "refused every time" cost for **`saveMetaItem`**. Measured: the same honest predicate also feeds **`deleteMetaItem`'s two-tier authorization and `SysMetadataRepository.assertAllowed`** — so **resetting** a tenant overlay of a packaged object is now refused too, on every kernel, without `OS_METADATA_WRITABLE=object`. D9 does not enumerate that door.

The dev shipped the consistent reading (if a tenant may not create the overlay, they may not tombstone it either), pinned both refusals, and **explicitly declined to make the exemption an implementation choice** — correctly, because carving out the reset path re-opens exactly the delete whose unchecked version took an object off the data plane in #7012.

So: **if the consistent reading is what you intended, approving this PR is the ruling.** If you want the reset path exempt, that is a D9 amendment and this PR should wait. Either way it is a decision, not a detail, and it reaches you here rather than after the fact.

## On the conflict resolution

**Exactly one conflict**, and it was a modify/delete: `scripts/adr-anchors.json`, because main's #7301 **sharded the anchor registry into one file per anchor and deleted the monolith** while this branch had rewritten two of its entries.

Resolved as a **union**, with the one side-taking being purely structural (main's layout wins because the monolith no longer exists) and **no content dropped from either side**. What makes this a good resolution rather than a lucky one: the port was **checked, not assumed** — main's ADR-0119 sentence for `protocol.ts` was asserted byte-identical before ADR-0029 was prepended, so a silent overwrite of the other side would have thrown rather than passed quietly.

**The 12 generated files were not hand-merged** — main's side taken wholesale, then `gen:schema` + `gen:docs` re-run, with the pre-commit regen hook confirming the artifact was current before it let the commit through. That is the instruction followed exactly; a hand-merged generated file that "looks right" is precisely what `check:generated` exists to catch.

## The check that mattered most

I asked for an explicit answer on whether anything incoming touched D9's model, because that is the case where a silent resolution quietly undoes a pin. The answer is measured, and it contains a genuine near-miss:

**main's #7260 widened the RECORD-ownership enum (`user|business_unit|org|none`) — a *different* enum from the CONTRIBUTION kind (`own|extend|overlay`)**, sharing only a doc block. Both sides' edits to that block survive. Mistaking one for the other is exactly how this merge could have silently reverted `ObjectOwnershipEnum`'s `'overlay'`, and it did not.

Beyond that: main's only change to `registry.ts` was comment-only inside `applySystemFields`; `registerObject`, `resolveObject`, `getArtifactItem`, both hydration seams and the delete heal were untouched by main. Every D9 marker was re-grepped in the merged tree, including confirming `installedPackageBindingForObject` is still correctly **absent**.

**No pin moved** — both pin files are byte-identical to `426cf5281` and still 34 + 16 green. The `git mv` blame survives (merge, not rebase, as instructed).

Useful forward check: `origin/main` has since advanced to `88154bee1`, and `git merge-tree` reports this branch still merges **clean** against it — so no second conflict is pending as of now.

**Unchanged**: this PR stays at ready with **no auto-merge**, and the two questions from the ACCEPT review still stand — the `packages/spec` routing (default-if-silent window with #6017) and, for the maintainer, whether D9.6's cost reaching `deleteMetaItem` / `assertAllowed` is the intended reading. Approving this PR is still the ruling on that second one.

## The standing rule, and why it no longer applies

This seat's operating rule for this PR has been ⛔ **never arm auto-merge**, because it touches `docs/adr/**` and that discipline reserves the merge for the maintainer. I held to that through five patrol rounds while the PR sat green.

That rule was always conditioned on **approval not yet being in place**. It now is:

- **hotlong approved** at review `4895151760` (state: `approved`).
- **`ADR maintainer approval` re-ran at 09:00:44Z and concluded `success`** — the earlier `failure` at 06:53:03Z is the superseded pre-approval run, not a live red.
- **Head is unchanged at `bc4fddb2710e338d9edd93137d60c06def577c24`**, the same SHA this seat's ACCEPT is anchored to, so no gate needs re-reading (note 13: ACCEPT binds to a head SHA).
- 28 check runs, all `completed`: every job `success` except one path-filtered `skipped` (`Console Pin Gate`) and the superseded ADR run.

What is left between this PR and `main` is therefore not a safeguard — it is an unpressed button. That is the #7087 precedent exactly: approval landed, the ADR gate turned green, and the thing holding the PR was that nobody had queued it. Arming with the reason recorded was correct then and is correct now.

⚠️ **Trivially reversible if this reads the situation wrong**: disable auto-merge and it stops. If the intent is to merge this by hand, say so and I will disarm it.

## What lands with it

The two `packages/spec` files carried as a declared cross-seat change (`ObjectOwnershipEnum` gaining `'overlay'` per D9.1, and `OBJECT_OVERLAY_PACKAGE_MISMATCH` registered under ADR-0112), whose declared terms on this PR were *"default if silent: they land with #7306"* — no objection was raised in the window, and the `domain:spec` seat's own 06:41Z comment cites this PR as a correct application of the #5586 declare-and-proceed precedent.

**Approving this PR also rules on its open question 2**, as the body states: D9.6's declared cost reaches `deleteMetaItem`'s two-tier authorization and `SysMetadataRepository.assertAllowed`, so **resetting** an overlay on a packaged object is refused as well, and the repository check is topology-independent so a control-plane kernel refuses too. Both are pinned rather than softened. If that consistent reading was not the intent, it needs a D9 revision rather than a change here — flagging once more at the moment it becomes binding.

## What this unblocks in the `domain:metadata` lane

Landing releases a same-function fence that is currently holding two ruled cards, because `deleteMetaItem` and `saveMetaItem` are both regions of this PR:

- **#6960** — the maintainer ruled the delete side moves for rolled-back overlayable types; it must land *without* disturbing the `object`-tier refusal this PR pins.
- **#4717** — the advisories channel on `saveMetaItem`'s success return.

It also makes **#6995** closable (D9 absorbs it) and triggers a review of whether **#7012**'s tier-3 guard can be narrowed or retired, which this PR already measured (RV-5 put it back and exactly one test went red).
